claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was born c. 185 and died c. 254.
Origen was the most important theologian and biblical scholar of the early Greek church.
Origen was a native of Alexandria.
Origen's homilies on Isaiah were originally delivered between 245 and 248.
Origen's homilies on Isaiah are extant only in a fourth-century Latin translation.
St. Jerome is the likely translator of the homilies on Isaiah into Latin, though he does not identify himself as the translator, likely because of controversies.
Jerome translated Origen's fourteen homilies on Ezekiel into Latin.
Jerome translated the homilies on Ezekiel at the request of a friend, taking care to preserve Origen's style and the simplicity of language beneficial for the Churches.
Origen prepared his Commentaries on Isaiah and on Ezekiel about the time of the reign of Gordian (238–244).
Eusebius records that Origen wrote thirty books of commentary on Isaiah, extending to Isaiah 30:6.
Eusebius records that Origen wrote twenty-five books of commentary on Ezekiel.
